input: This capital appraisal examines a proposed bottling line and returns a net present value of $88k. The installed cost of the line is $717k, and the expected net saving is estimated at $140k per year for 8 years. When these savings are discounted at 8%, they have a present value of $805k, which means that the present value of the savings exceeds the installed cost, with the excess representing a net present value of $88k. It is important to note that the appraisal is expressed in today's money, in the sense that the discounting converts each year's saving into the sum that, if it were held now, would be equivalent to it, and the net present value is what remains once the cost of the line itself has been charged against those converted savings. A positive figure indicates that the project returns more than the rate used to discount it. Furthermore, the case rests heavily on the saving figure: an annual saving that is held at $140k over the full term supports the result, whereas a saving that fell short of the estimate would pull the present value of $805k down towards the installed cost. It should also be noted that these savings are vendor and utility estimates, and no saving has yet been measured on a comparable installation, so the $88k margin is essentially an estimate built on estimates, which would be confirmed or lost during the first years of operation, when the actual saving can be compared with the $140k per year that the appraisal assumes.
